name: PassMark: Memory Mark
description: A composite score of PassMark's Database and Memory test cases, also factoring in the amount of available RAM.
note: This benchmark does not scale well on instances with more than 16 vCPUs. Empirical data shows measured scores plateau and may even degrade as vCPU count increases, so it is not recommended for evaluating larger instance sizes. The score also depends on the amount of RAM that was free when the test started (the exact formula is not published by PassMark), which can differ between runs on the same instance type. In our measurements the Memory Mark changed by up to 43% between runs while the underlying memory speed subtests stayed within about 5%, so prefer the individual memory tests to compare raw memory performance.

environment_fields.duration: Duration (seconds) of the benchmarking framework run that produced this score, shared by all benchmarks and configs of that run.
environment_fields.measured_at: Timestamp (UTC) of finishing the benchmark run.
environment_fields.kernel_version: Linux kernel version of the server running the benchmark (not recorded for managed databases).
